newsitem.title: DUBAI: Manila checking on 16 Filipinos jailed in Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Manila checking on 16 Filipinos jailed in Saudi.

text.p: The Philippines' vice-president will travel to Saudi Arabia this week to discuss the fate of 16 Filipinos imprisoned in the kingdom after staging a protest, an official said on Tuesday.

"The reason Mr (Joseph) Estrada is going to Saudi Arabia is to get the complete facts about the case," Estrada's communications director Reli German told Reuters during a visit to the United Arab Emirates by Estrada.
German is accompanying the vice-president on a regional tour.

"What we have so far is that these Filipinos were protesting for something -- we don't know what -- in front of the Philippines embassy (in Riyadh)," he said. "A report was filed with the authorities and the protesters were picked up."
German said he did not know exactly when the protest had taken place, but believed it was during the last month.

Reports said the arrested Filipinos were among 600 Philippines nationals stranded in Saudi Arabia who could not afford to get home because they quit jobs with local employers before their contracts expired.
About four million Filipinos work overseas, many of them in the Gulf, in hopes of making more money in the oil-rich states than they can at home.
"Hundreds of Filipinos are stranded in Saudi Arabia," German said.

"If they finish their regular term of employment, the employer normally provides them with transportation back home. But if they do not...they are stranded and don't have the money to buy the tickets," he said.

German said Filipinos were also stranded in the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia's neighbour to the east. A UAE amnesty for illegal foreign workers expired on November 1, but diplomats say many of the unlawful workers remain.
"Today (Tuesday), there was a couple here in Abu Dhabi who did not finish their contract with their employer because they were being maltreated," German said.
"The records show that they were indeed being maltreated and they were stranded here. The vice-president gave them tickets back home," he said.
About 85,000 Filipinos work in the UAE.

The UAE came under international criticism last year when a court sentenced Filipina maid Sarah Balabagan to death for stabbing her 70-year-old employer to death. She claimed he had tried to rape her.

UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan intervened and presuaded the victim's family to drop the demand for a death sentence in exchange for blood money. Balabagan returned to the Philippines in August after serving nine months of a one-year jail sentence.
